scenes.say: What keeps your network logins secure? How does Active Directory actually work?

scenes.label: Directory
scenes.sub: Stores users, computers, and groups in one place.
scenes.say: Active Directory is a directory. It stores users, computers, and groups all in one place.

rows.b: DCs sync changes to each other

scenes.say: A domain controller authenticates logins. Replication keeps all controllers in sync. Policy means permissions and settings come from AD.

scenes.title: AD in Action
scenes.say: You can search for locked accounts, unlock users, or list group members with simple commands.

scenes.question: How many DCs should you run?
scenes.right: Always run at least two for redundancy.
scenes.say: Interview trap: How many domain controllers should you run? Never just one—always at least two for redundancy.
